What happened, component by component

Chapters

Each month is labelled Build (fixes under 40% of commits) or Harden (40% or more). Neighbouring months with the same label join into one chapter.

Rhythm

Commits per week, per year. Dark = quiet, bright = busy.

Where it lives in code

Functions touched most often by this feature.

Every commit

A fix, from bug to every branch

Pick a fix. Each one names the commit that caused it with a Fixes: line, so we can measure how long the bug lived, how long the fix took, and which branches got it.

Every fix, every branch

Gap board

Fixes whose bug reached a branch but whose fix never did. This is the 13.1 → 12.5 question, answered for every fix at once.

How long bugs hide, by component

Bug lifetime

From the commit that caused the bug to the fix being written. Log scale. Each dot is a fix; the white tick is the median.

Written → applied

How long patches wait between author date and commit date. Minutes to years.

Fix share over time

Per quarter. When fixes overtake features, the code is in hardening.

Fixes that needed fixing

How it works

Like a robot's flight recorder

A robot logs every joint and sensor with a timestamp so you can replay a fall frame by frame. Git already logs every change to every file with two timestamps: when the patch was written, and when it was applied. This view replays that log, at any zoom, filtered to one feature or one bug.

Rules, all visible

  1. Component comes from the file path (mac.c → mac80211 glue, wmi* → WMI, dp_rx* → Datapath RX, and so on). A commit sits in every lane it touched, sized by lines changed there.
  2. Kind comes from the subject: a Fixes: line or words like fix, leak, race, crash → fix; add, support, enable → feature; refactor, move, rename, remove → refactor; Revert → revert.
  3. Feature = commits whose subject or message matches the story's pattern. Type your own pattern to build any timeline.
  4. Chapters = months labelled by fix share, joined when neighbours agree. The first 5% of commits are Inception.
  5. CR journey = the Fixes: line gives the bug's birth commit. Branch presence comes from the backport mapping (stable "commit X upstream" lines here; on your tree: patch-id, cherry-pick lines, CR id, then subject).

Limits: a regex finds commits that say the word, not every commit that changed the behaviour. Kind is a heuristic. Bug lifetime counts only fixes whose Fixes: target is in this data.

Run it on 12.5 and 13.1

python3 engine/timeline.py git --repo ~/qsdk/wlan-host \
  --path drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath12k \
  --branch 13.1=origin/r13.1 --branch 12.5=origin/r12.5 --main 13.1 \
  --out ui/timeline/timeline.json
node ui/timeline/build.js ui/timeline/timeline.json ui/timeline/CLDI-time-machine.html

Everything stays on your machine. With two branches, every CR journey shows when the fix reached 12.5, or a red gap with its age if it never did.
